newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Senate leader backs $1.7 bln bridge bond.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Senate leader backs $1.7 bln bridge bond.

text.p: California's Senate president favors placing a $1.7 billion bond measure before the voters to pay for reinforcing the San Francisco Bay area's bridges against earthquakes, according to a report Friday.

Senate President Pro Tem Bill Lockyer, a Democrat, said the bond measure would be written so that if voters reject it, all the bridge reinforcement costs would be borne by the state, the San Francisco Chronicle reported.
Lockyer said he now supported the bond measure because southern California lawmakers have refused to cut a deal to cover the costs of bridge repair and replacement.
"A 50-50 cost split is no longer acceptable," Lockyer said. "The only alternative I see is a bond measure."
